package_info.why_malicious: N/A – JFrog Frogbot is not malicious. It is a legitimate security tool designed to proactively detect and alert on secrets exposure in code repositories. No malicious code or behavior is described in the provided report.

behavioral_signatures: Automated scanning of pull requests for secrets immediately after PR creation.
Periodic scanning of entire repositories for exposed secrets.
Email notification to committers when secrets are detected, originating from frogbot@service.jfrog.com.
file_indicators: Presence of plaintext secrets (API keys, credentials, tokens) in source code files.
Files containing secrets such as .py, .js, .env, and configuration files (e.g., config.js, settings.py).
network_indicators: Outbound email notifications sent from frogbot@service.jfrog.com.
No suspicious or unauthorized external network communication described.
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for automated scanning activity on pull requests and repositories, and for email notifications about detected secrets from frogbot@service.jfrog.com. Look for patterns of secrets exposure in code, such as API keys or credentials in plaintext within source files. No malicious activity is present; this is a legitimate security tool.
